correctness.rationale: The β(p^a)/p^a identity p/(p+1)+(-1)^a/((p+1)p^a) gives lower bounds 1-1/p, and enhanced 20/27 for 3^a,a>=2, 104/125 for 5^a,a>=2. Tóth square-gcd counting shows β(n)<n-1 for composite n!=4, hence K=(n-1)/β(n) integer >=2. For even n, all odd-prime exponents must be even because β(n)|odd n-1; if ω<=4, β(n)/n>=105/384>1/4 so odd K=3; this excludes 3|n, gives β(n)/n>=385/1152>1/3, contradiction. For odd n, smallest-prime products force K<2 except 3*5*r with r in 7,11,13; this forces K=2 and 3-exponent 1. Mod4 eliminates r=13; parity of r=7 or 11 exponent forced odd, with β(7^odd) divisible by3 excluding r=7. For r=11, 5-exponent must 1 by 416/825>1/2; β(11^odd) divisible by5, contradiction. Prime powers and lower omega included. Independently verified the sharp rational barriers and initial prime-power values. Universal conclusion uses inequalities, not finite search.

value.rationale: The least number of distinct primes is a canonical obstruction for Lehmer-type compositeness problems. Proving that any odd counterexample must have at least four and any even counterexample at least five distinct primes, for unrestricted exponents, eliminates large natural classes in Tóth’s named open divisibility problem. It is a structural necessary condition, not the false claim of solving the unrestricted problem.

limitations: Only necessary prime-support conditions; excludes no existence for omega>=4 odd or >=5 even.
Finite checker cannot prove infinite absence of other composite solutions.
